qe: The Government of India Act, 1919 contained a statutory provision for appointing a review commission ten years from its date of enactment. Which British Prime Minister prematurely constituted this seven-member commission in November 1927?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1919 में इसके अधिनियमन की तारीख से दस वर्ष बाद एक समीक्षा आयोग नियुक्त करने का वैधानिक प्रावधान शामिल था। किस ब्रिटिश प्रधानमंत्री ने नवंबर 1927 में समय से पहले इस सात सदस्यीय आयोग का गठन किया था?
o: Stanley Baldwin
Winston Churchill
John Morley
Ramsay MacDonald
e: Detailed Explanation: The Indian Statutory Commission, popularly known as the Simon Commission, was prematurely appointed on November 8, 1927, by British Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin to prevent the crucial question of Indian constitutional reforms from falling into the hands of the opposition Labour Party.

qe: By the mid-1920s, the unworkable nature of Dyarchy led to various inquiries. Which specific colonial commission investigated the critical failure of the Raj to recruit an adequate number of British officers for the administrative services?
qh: 1920 के दशक के मध्य तक, द्वैध शासन (Dyarchy) की अव्यवहारिक प्रकृति के कारण विभिन्न जाँचें हुईं। किस विशिष्ट औपनिवेशिक आयोग ने प्रशासनिक सेवाओं के लिए पर्याप्त संख्या में ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों की भर्ती करने में राज की विफलता की जाँच की थी?
o: The Lee Commission
The Muddiman Commission
The Linlithgow Commission
The Rowlatt Commission
e: Detailed Explanation: In the mid-1920s, several reports evaluated the 1919 Act. The Lee Commission specifically investigated the failure to recruit sufficient British officers for the imperial administrative services, while Muddiman looked into diarchic deadlocks and Linlithgow into agriculture.

qe: Which Conservative Secretary of State for India was responsible for appointing the Simon Commission, frequently taunting Indian politicians for their alleged inability to draft an agreed constitutional scheme?
qh: भारत के लिए कौन सा कंजर्वेटिव राज्य सचिव (Secretary of State) साइमन आयोग की नियुक्ति के लिए जिम्मेदार था, जो अक्सर भारतीय राजनेताओं को एक सहमत संवैधानिक योजना तैयार करने में उनकी कथित असमर्थता के लिए ताना मारता था?
o: Lord Birkenhead
Edwin Montagu
John Morley
Viceroy Lord Minto
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Birkenhead, the Conservative Secretary of State for India, masterminded the appointment of the all-white Simon Commission. He constantly taunted Indians, claiming they were incapable of formulating a concrete constitutional plan supported by wide sections of local political opinion.

qe: What primary intellectual and political grievance unified almost all Indian factions to immediately boycott and oppose the Indian Statutory Commission upon its announcement in 1927?
qh: 1927 में भारतीय वैधानिक आयोग (Simon Commission) की घोषणा के बाद लगभग सभी भारतीय गुटों को तुरंत इसका बहिष्कार और विरोध करने के लिए किस प्राथमिक बौद्धिक और राजनीतिक शिकायत ने एकजुट किया था?
o: The complete exclusion of Indians from the commission and the underlying notion that foreigners would judge India's fitness for self-government
The mandatory requirement to enforce English-only education codes across all rural ashrams
The total legal abolition of the separate communal electorates allocated to non-Asian foreign settlers
The dynamic implementation of a metabolic tax surcharge on all native cotton textile mills
e: Detailed Explanation: The exclusion of Indians from an all-white commission tasking with deciding India's constitutional future was seen as a deliberate insult to national self-respect and a blatant violation of the principle of self-determination, triggering immediate and nearly unanimous opposition.

qe: The Indian National Congress formally resolved to boycott the Simon Commission 'at every stage and in every form' during its December 1927 annual session. Where was this historic session hosted, and who presided over it?
qh: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने दिसंबर 1927 के अपने वार्षिक सत्र के दौरान साइमन आयोग का 'हर स्तर पर और हर रूप में' बहिष्कार करने का औपचारिक प्रस्ताव पारित किया। यह ऐतिहासिक सत्र कहाँ आयोजित किया गया था, और इसकी अध्यक्षता किसने की थी?
o: The Madras session under Dr. M.A. Ansari
The Calcutta session under Dadabhai Naoroji
The Nagpur session under W.C. Bonnerjee
The Belgaum session under Mahatma Gandhi
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress met in a highly charged atmosphere at Madras in December 1927 under the presidency of Dr. M.A. Ansari. The session resolved to completely boycott the Simon Commission and passed a snap resolution declaring complete independence as the ultimate goal.

qe: The announcement of the Simon Commission fractured the All India Muslim League into two competing factions in 1927. Which faction decided to oppose the commission, and where did they convene?
qh: साइमन कमीशन की घोषणा ने 1927 में अखिल भारतीय मुस्लिम लीग को दो प्रतिस्पर्धी गुटों में विभाजित कर दिया। किस गुट ने आयोग का विरोध करने का निर्णय लिया और वे कहाँ एकत्र हुए?
o: The faction under Mohammad Ali Jinnah at Calcutta
The faction under Muhammad Shafi at Lahore
The Aligarh conservative school network at Delhi
The Faraizi revolutionary council at East Bengal
e: Detailed Explanation: In 1927, the Muslim League split over the Simon Commission issue. The majority faction led by Mohammad Ali Jinnah met at Calcutta and resolved to boycott the commission, while a conservative faction under Muhammad Shafi met at Lahore to support the government.

qe: The Simon Commission landed at Bombay on February 3, 1928, facing nationwide black flag demonstrations and 'Simon Go Back' slogans. Which two young leaders emerged at the forefront of this new wave of youth and student mobilization?
qh: साइमन कमीशन 3 फरवरी, 1928 को बॉम्बे पहुंचा, जिसे देशव्यापी काले झंडे के प्रदर्शनों और 'साइमन गो बैक' के नारों का सामना करना पड़ा। युवा और छात्र लामबंदी की इस नई लहर में कौन से दो युवा नेता सबसे आगे उभरे?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Rajendra Prasad
C. Rajagopalachari and M.A. Ansari
Lala Lajpat Rai and Madan Mohan Malaviya
e: Detailed Explanation: The anti-Simon upsurge energized a new generation of youth. Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose emerged as the prominent leaders of this radical student wave, traveling extensively to organize militant protest leagues across the country.

qe: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was appointed by the Bombay Legislative Council to work with the Simon Commission. When he went before the commission in October 1928, what radical constitutional rights did he demand for all citizens?
qh: डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर को बॉम्बे विधान परिषद द्वारा साइमन कमीशन के साथ काम करने के लिए नियुक्त किया गया था। जब वे अक्टूबर 1928 में आयोग के सामने गए, तो उन्होंने सभी नागरिकों के लिए किन क्रांतिकारी संवैधानिक अधिकारों की मांग की?
o: Universal adult franchise for both males and females alike, provincial autonomy, and dyarchy at the Center
Separate electorates based strictly on hereditary caste Pure purity lines for high-caste Hindus
The complete legislative termination of the bicameral Central Legislative Assembly
Restricting voting franchise exclusively to landowners who paid a cash revenue surcharge
e: Detailed Explanation: Before the Simon Commission in October 1928, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar made a highly progressive demand for 'universal adult franchise' for men and women alike, a right that was not yet guaranteed in most contemporary European nations, along with provincial autonomy.

qe: On behalf of the Bahishkrita Hitakarini Sabha, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar submitted a detailed memorandum to the Simon Commission. What was his central assertion regarding the socio-political status of the Depressed Classes?
qh: बहिष्कृत हितकारिणी सभा की ओर से, डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर ने साइमन कमीशन को एक विस्तृत ज्ञापन सौंपा। दलित वर्गों (Depressed Classes) की सामाजिक-राजनीतिक स्थिति के संबंध में उनका मुख्य दावा क्या था?
o: There was no link between the depressed classes and the Hindu community, and they should be regarded as a distinct and independent minority
They formed an un-splintered, identical religious block with orthodox upper-caste Brahmins
They possessed absolute land ownership rights over 100% of the Permanent Settlement tracts
They required the mandatory implementation of Sanskritic education frameworks inside rural subdivisions
e: Detailed Explanation: Dr. Ambedkar's memorandum asserted that the Depressed Classes had no organic socio-religious link with the mainstream Hindu community and should be legally treated as a distinct, independent minority requiring specific political safeguards.

qe: What specific political protection guidelines did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar demand for the Depressed Classes if the colonial state refused to grant universal adult franchise?
qh: यदि औपनिवेशिक राज्य सार्वभौमिक वयस्क मताधिकार देने से इनकार करता है, तो डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर ने दलित वर्गों के लिए किस विशिष्ट राजनीतिक सुरक्षा दिशानिर्देश की मांग की थी?
o: A campaign for a separate electorate for the depressed classes and representation on the same basis as the Mohammedan minority
The total legal abolition of any reserved seats inside the provincial assemblies
The complete administrative transfer of the district collector's magisterial powers to village elders
An absolute restriction barring lower-caste individuals from entering public services
e: Detailed Explanation: Ambedkar argued that due to social enslavement and economic poverty, the Depressed Classes needed greater protection than any other minority. He demanded representation equal to the Muslim minority: reserved seats if universal franchise was granted, or separate electorates if it was denied.

qe: The report published by the Simon Commission did grant reserved seats to the Depressed Classes, but what restrictive condition did it attach that highly displeased Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?
qh: साइमन कमीशन द्वारा प्रकाशित रिपोर्ट ने दलित वर्गों के लिए आरक्षित सीटें तो दीं, लेकिन उसने कौन सी प्रतिबंधात्मक शर्त जोड़ी जिससे डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर अत्यधिक असंतुष्ट हुए?
o: Candidates who would take part in the elections would have to get their competence endorsed by the provincial Governor first
All lower-caste candidates were legally forced to undergo specialized military arsenal testing examinations in English
The seats were restricted exclusively to those who paid a heavy land revenue tax surcharge directly to London
The elected representatives were barred from asking any supplementary budget questions inside the council rooms
e: Detailed Explanation: Although the Simon Commission report allocated reserved seats to the Depressed Classes, it watered down the concession by requiring candidates to get a certificate of competence endorsed by the British Governor, which Ambedkar strongly opposed.

qe: The widespread youth upsurge against the Simon Commission provided a fertile ground for the germination of radical socialist ideas. Which of the following radical organizations emerged or spread during this phase?
qh: साइमन कमीशन के खिलाफ व्यापक युवा उभार ने कट्टरपंथी समाजवादी विचारों के प्रसार के लिए एक उपजाऊ जमीन प्रदान की। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कट्टरपंथी संगठन इस चरण के दौरान उभरा या फैला?
o: Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha, Workers' and Peasants' Parties, and Hindustani Sewa Dal (Karnataka)
Atmiya Sabha, Dharma Sabha, and the Tattvabodhini Sabha core platforms
The Ladies Social Conference and the All India Women’s Conference branches
The Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company and the Satyashodhak Labour Front
e: Detailed Explanation: The mass anti-Simon protests catalyzed socialist groups across multiple regions, leading directly to the expansion and prominence of groups like the Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha, regional Workers' and Peasants' Parties, and the Hindustani Sewa Dal in Karnataka.

qe: During the intense police crackdowns on peaceful anti-Simon demonstrations, which iconic nationalist leader received severe, fatal blows to his chest in October 1928, leading to his tragic demise on November 17, 1828?
qh: साइमन-विरोधी शांतिपूर्ण प्रदर्शनों पर पुलिस की कड़ी कार्रवाई के दौरान, अक्टूबर 1928 में किस प्रतिष्ठित राष्ट्रवादी नेता के सीने पर गंभीर और घातक लाठियां लगीं, जिससे 17 नवंबर, 1928 को उनका दुखद निधन हो गया?
o: Lala Lajpat Rai
Govind Ballabh Pant
Jawaharlal Nehru
Bhagat Singh
e: Detailed Explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai (Sher-i-Punjab) led a peaceful anti-Simon procession in Lahore in October 1928. He was brutally assaulted during an unprovoked police lathi-charge, sustaining severe chest injuries that directly caused his death on November 17, 1928.

qe: The Simon Commission recommendations published in a two-volume report in May 1930 proposed a major structural change for provincial administration. What did it recommend regarding Dyarchy?
qh: मई 1930 में दो खंडों की रिपोर्ट में प्रकाशित साइमन कमीशन की सिफारिशों ने प्रांतीय प्रशासन के लिए एक बड़े संरचनात्मक परिवर्तन का प्रस्ताव दिया। द्वैध शासन (Dyarchy) के संबंध में इसने क्या सिफारिश की थी?
o: The complete abolition of dyarchy and the establishment of representative government and autonomy in the provinces
The structural consolidation of dyarchy by transferring law and order to bureaucratic executive councillors permanently
Subordinating all provincial transferred subjects directly to a special three-judge panel of the High Court
The total legal transfer of provincial revenue collection rights to the village caste elders
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon Commission report recommended completely scraping the unworkable system of Dyarchy in the provinces. In its place, it proposed establishing representative governance, granting a form of provincial autonomy to the local administrations.

qe: Under the provincial autonomy model suggested by the Simon Commission, what overarching discretionary power was explicitly reserved for the British Governor?
qh: साइमन कमीशन द्वारा सुझाए गए प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता मॉडल के तहत, ब्रिटिश राज्यपाल के लिए कौन सी सर्वोपरि विवेकाधीन शक्ति (discretionary power) स्पष्ट रूप से सुरक्षित थी?
o: Discretionary powers in relation to internal security and administrative powers to protect different communities
The absolute right to independently print regional currencies without central tracking guidelines
The sovereign authority to appoint the Prime Minister of Great Britain independent of Parliament
Complete operational command over the logistical shipping lines operating along the western coast
e: Detailed Explanation: While recommending provincial autonomy, the Simon report inserted imperial safeguards. It recommended arming the Governor with wide discretionary powers over internal security and specialized administrative authority to protect minorities.

qe: What stance did the May 1930 Simon Commission report adopt regarding parliamentary responsibility and executive appointments at the central government level?
qh: मई 1930 की साइमन कमीशन की रिपोर्ट ने केंद्र सरकार के स्तर पर संसदीय जवाबदेही और कार्यकारी नियुक्तियों के संबंध में क्या रुख अपनाया?
o: It completely rejected parliamentary responsibility at the centre, giving the Governor-General absolute power to appoint cabinet members
It introduced a full responsible government framework with cabinet ministers answerable to the lower house majority
It mandated that at least half of the central executive council seats must be elected by village panchayats
It completely subordinated the executive authority of the Governor-General to the Federal Court benches
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon Commission refused to grant democratic advance at the all-India level. It rejected any introduction of parliamentary responsibility at the center, ensuring the Governor-General retained autocratic control to select and appoint his cabinet.

qe: Regarding the judicial framework, what structural recommendation did the Simon Commission outline concerning the relationship between the Government of India and the higher judiciary?
qh: न्यायिक ढांचे के संबंध में, साइमन कमीशन ने भारत सरकार और उच्च न्यायपालिका के बीच संबंधों को लेकर कौन सा संरचनात्मक सुझाव दिया था?
o: The Government of India would have complete control over the High Court
The High Courts were to be made entirely independent and placed under the Privy Council exclusively
All High Court judicial decisions had to be cleared by the legislative council non-officials majority
The total legal abolition of any High Court infrastructure across Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras
e: Detailed Explanation: To centralize administrative grip, the Simon Commission report recommended that the colonial Government of India should exercise complete administrative control over the provincial High Courts.

qe: What recommendation did the Simon Commission report make regarding the retention of separate communal electorates and the expansion of mass franchise?
qh: साइमन कमीशन की रिपोर्ट ने पृथक सांप्रदायिक निर्वाचन क्षेत्रों को बनाए रखने और जन मताधिकार के विस्तार के संबंध में क्या सिफारिश की थी?
o: Separate communal electorates should be retained and extended to other communities, and there was to be no universal franchise
Separate electorates were to be completely abolished in favor of universal adult suffrage for all men and women
Communal electorates were to be restricted strictly to wealthy urban zamindars who paid a cash income tax
The implementation of a separate electorate framework exclusively for the landless untouchable agricultural laborers
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon report rejected Dr. Ambedkar's demand for democracy. It stated that separate communal electorates must be retained and extended to other communities until tensions died down, and it explicitly opposed introducing universal adult franchise.

qe: To manage the structural integration of the sub-continent, what transitional administrative entity did the Simon Commission suggest establishing to include both British provinces and princely states?
qh: उपमहाद्वीप के संरचनात्मक एकीकरण को प्रबंधित करने के लिए, साइमन कमीशन ने ब्रिटिश प्रांतों और रियासतों दोनों को शामिल करने के लिए किस संक्रमणकालीन प्रशासनिक इकाई की स्थापना का सुझाव दिया था?
o: A Consultative Council of Greater India
The Congress Working Committee alliance trust
The Federal Court Arbitration Assembly
The United States of South Asia corporate board
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon Commission accepted the concept of federalism only as a distant goal. It suggested an intermediate step: creating a 'Consultative Council of Greater India' containing representatives from both the British-governed provinces and the native princely states.

qe: The Simon Commission recommended distinct territorial reorganizations for the western and northwestern boundaries of British India. Which of the following matches these recommendations?
qh: साइमन कमीशन ने ब्रिटिश भारत की पश्चिमी और उत्तर-पश्चिमी सीमाओं के लिए अलग-अलग क्षेत्रीय पुनर्गठन की सिफारिश की थी। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा इन सिफारिशों का मिलान करता है?
o: Sindh should be separated from Bombay, Burma separated from India, and legislatures set up in NWFP and Baluchistan
Bihar and Orissa should be completely merged back into the Bengal Presidency delta plains
The Punjab plains should be separated and appended directly to the Central Provinces administrative circle
The total administrative integration of the Kingdom of Nepal into the United Provinces layout
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon report proposed key boundary adjustments: separating Sindh from the Bombay Presidency, separating Burma from British India completely (as it was not a natural part of the subcontinent), and granting local legislatures to the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP) and Baluchistan.

qe: As an answer to Lord Birkenhead’s arrogant challenge, an All Parties Conference met in February 1928 and appointed a sub-committee to draft a constitution. Who served as the Chairman of this historic sub-committee?
qh: लॉर्ड बर्कनहेड की अहंकारी चुनौती के जवाब में, फरवरी 1928 में एक सर्वदलीय सम्मेलन (All Parties Conference) बुलाकर एक संविधान का मसौदा तैयार करने के लिए एक उप-समिति नियुक्त की गई। इस ऐतिहासिक उप-समिति के अध्यक्ष कौन थे?
o: Motilal Nehru
Jawaharlal Nehru
Tej Bahadur Sapru
Subhash Chandra Bose
e: Detailed Explanation: The challenge to produce an agreed constitution was accepted by Indian leaders. The All Parties Conference appointed a sub-committee chaired by Pandit Motilal Nehru to draft India's first indigenous constitutional framework, known as the Nehru Report.

qe: The members of the Motilal Nehru sub-committee drafted a comprehensive constitutional framework by August 1928. Which of the following sets represents the prominent members who worked on this committee?
qh: मोतीलाल नेहरू उप-समिति के सदस्यों ने अगस्त 1928 तक एक व्यापक संवैधानिक ढांचे का मसौदा तैयार किया। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा सेट उन प्रमुख सदस्यों का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है जिन्होंने इस समिति में काम किया था?
o: Tej Bahadur Sapru, Subhash Bose, M.S. Aney, Mangal Singh, Ali Imam, Shuab Qureshi, and G.R. Pradhan
Mohammad Ali Jinnah, Muhammad Shafi, Nawab Salimullah, and the Agha Khan exclusively
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Chimanlal Setalvad, Jagat Narayan, and Sultan Ahmad Khan
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Narahari Parikh, Mohanlal Pandya, and Ravi Shankar Vyas
e: Detailed Explanation: The Nehru Committee was composed of a cross-section of political minds, including legal and political experts like Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru, Subhash Chandra Bose, M.S. Aney, Mangal Singh, Ali Imam, Shuab Qureshi, and G.R. Pradhan.

qe: The recommendations of the 1928 Nehru Committee were completely unanimous except for one critical baseline issue that created a division within the nationalist ranks. What was this issue?
qh: 1928 की नेहरू समिति की सिफारिशें एक महत्वपूर्ण बुनियादी मुद्दे को छोड़कर पूरी तरह से सर्वसम्मत थीं, जिसने राष्ट्रवादी रैंकों के भीतर एक विभाजन पैदा कर दिया था। यह मुद्दा क्या था?
o: The majority favored 'Dominion Status' as the basis of the Constitution, while a younger section demanded 'Complete Independence'
A fierce disagreement over whether to completely abolish the system of private land property in land
Whether to restrict the voting franchise exclusively to the high-caste educated Brahmins
The inclusion of English as the mandatory official language across all lower subdivision court rooms
e: Detailed Explanation: The main point of contention in the Nehru Report was the ultimate goal. The older majority section led by Motilal Nehru favored 'Dominion Status' within the empire, while a younger, radical section led by Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhash Bose vigorously demanded that 'Complete Independence' (Purna Swaraj) be the core basis.

qe: The historic 1928 Nehru Report restricted its immediate constitutional proposals strictly to British India, but it explicitly envisaged what future structural link-up with the native Princely States?
qh: ऐतिहासिक 1928 की नेहरू रिपोर्ट ने अपने तत्काल संवैधानिक प्रस्तावों को कड़ाई से ब्रिटिश भारत तक सीमित रखा, लेकिन इसने देशी रियासतों (Princely States) के साथ भविष्य के किस संरचनात्मक जुड़ाव की परिकल्पना की थी?
o: A link-up on a federal basis
A complete permanent military annexation layout
The total absolute structural integration into the Bengal presidency
An informal trading alliance channel managed by British managing agencies
e: Detailed Explanation: The Nehru Report looked toward an integrated future for the subcontinent, explicitly proposing that a free British India should link up with the native princely states on a comprehensive federal framework.

qe: The 1928 Nehru Report took a radical step by completely rejecting separate electorates. What alternative electoral system did it propose to safeguard minority representations?
qh: 1928 की नेहरू रिपोर्ट ने पृथक निर्वाचन मंडल को पूरी तरह से खारिज करके एक क्रांतिकारी कदम उठाया। अल्पसंख्यक प्रतिनिधित्व की रक्षा के लिए इसने कौन सी वैकल्पिक चुनावी प्रणाली प्रस्तावित की थी?
o: Joint electorates with reservation of seats for Muslims at the Centre and in provinces where they were in a minority
Separate communal electorates extended to all intermediate non-Brahmin caste configurations
An open universal adult franchise tracking system with zero reserved seats for any community
A class-based indirect electoral college managed exclusively by local village panchayats
e: Detailed Explanation: The Nehru Report rejected separate electorates as divisive. In their place, it demanded a system of joint electorates across India, supplemented by reservation of seats for Muslims at the center and in provinces where they formed a numerical minority (and not where they were in a majority, like Punjab or Bengal).

qe: How many 'Fundamental Rights' were explicitly outlined and demanded for citizens within the historic constitutional draft of the 1928 Nehru Report?
qh: 1928 की नेहरू रिपोर्ट के ऐतिहासिक संवैधानिक मसौदे के भीतर नागरिकों के लिए कितने 'मौलिक अधिकार' (Fundamental Rights) विशेष रूप से रेखांकित और मांगे गए थे?
o: Nineteen fundamental rights
Seven fundamental rights
Ten fundamental rights
Exactly twelve fundamental rights
e: Detailed Explanation: The Nehru Report featured a highly progressive charter of civil liberties, explicitly demanding exactly nineteen fundamental rights for citizens, including universal adult suffrage, the right to form trade unions, and equal rights for women.

qe: According to the structural blueprints of the Nehru Report, what was the proposed legislative composition for the central Indian Parliament?
qh: नेहरू रिपोर्ट के संरचनात्मक खाके के अनुसार, केंद्रीय भारतीय संसद के लिए प्रस्तावित विधायी संरचना क्या थी?
o: A bicameral arrangement consisting of a 500-member House of Representatives and a 200-member Senate
A unicameral Imperial Legislative Assembly composed of 145 elected members exclusively
A tiered Council of State featuring 60 members nominated directly by the British Crown
A centralized assembly where seats were allocated strictly based on the military importance of provinces
e: Detailed Explanation: The Nehru Report recommended a democratic bicameral parliament at the center: a lower house named the House of Representatives consisting of 500 members elected via adult suffrage, and an upper house named the Senate featuring 200 members elected by provincial councils.

qe: What operational tenure durations were fixed by the 1928 Nehru Committee for the proposed central House of Representatives and the Senate respectively?
qh: 1928 की नेहरू समिति द्वारा प्रस्तावित केंद्रीय प्रतिनिधि सभा (House of Representatives) और सीनेट के लिए क्रमशः कितनी परिचालन अवधि तय की गई थी?
o: 5 years for the House of Representatives and 7 years for the Senate
3 years for the House of Representatives and 5 years for the Senate
5 years for both houses concurrent with the central budget apresentação list
A permanent lifelong tenure for the Senate and 1 year for the lower house
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the legislative hierarchy designed in the Nehru Report, the lower chamber (House of Representatives) was assigned an operational tenure of 5 years, while the upper chamber (Senate) was given a tenure of 7 years.

qe: Under the executive model designed by the Nehru Committee, the central government was to be headed by a Governor-General. How was this office to be funded and directed?
qh: नेहरू समिति द्वारा तैयार किए गए कार्यकारी मॉडल के तहत, केंद्र सरकार का प्रमुख एक गवर्नर-जनरल होना था। इस कार्यालय को कैसे वित्तपोषित और निर्देशित किया जाना था?
o: Appointed by the British government but paid out of Indian revenues, acting strictly on the advice of a central executive council responsible to the Parliament
Handpicked by the Federal Court judges and paid out of the savings of the Tilak Swaraj Fund
Financed entirely by the British exchequer in London and possessing absolute sovereign veto powers
Selected directly by a majority vote of the village panchayats and unaccountable to the legislature
e: Detailed Explanation: The report maintained a constitutional link with Britain by stating that the Governor-General would be appointed by the Crown. However, he would be paid out of Indian revenues and was legally bound to act as a constitutional head, guided entirely by the advice of an executive council responsible to the elected Parliament.

qe: Regarding secularism, what explicit core principle did the 1928 Nehru Report incorporate to ensure equality among all religious communities?
qh: धर्मनिरपेक्षता के संबंध में, 1928 की नेहरू रिपोर्ट ने सभी धार्मिक समुदायों के बीच समानता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए किस स्पष्ट मुख्य सिद्धांत को शामिल किया था?
o: Complete dissociation of the State from religion
The mandatory declaration of Hinduism as the official state religion
The structural management of all mosque assets by the central council
Granting special legislative veto privileges to religious ulema bodies
e: Detailed Explanation: Anticipating the secular framework of modern India, the Nehru Report explicitly recommended the 'complete dissociation of the State from religion', ensuring the future government would remain completely neutral in matters of faith.

qe: In December 1927, a large group of Muslim leaders met in Delhi and formulated a charter of demands to be incorporated into the draft constitution, which were accepted by the Congress Madras session. What is this historic charter called?
qh: दिसंबर 1927 में, मुस्लिम नेताओं के एक बड़े समूह ने दिल्ली में मुलाकात की और मसौदा संविधान में शामिल किए जाने वाले मांगों का एक चार्टर तैयार किया, जिसे कांग्रेस के मद्रास सत्र ने स्वीकार कर लिया। इस ऐतिहासिक चार्टर को क्या कहा जाता है?
o: The Delhi Proposals
The Simla Memorandum
The Aligarh Concord
The Lucknow Resolution
e: Detailed Explanation: In December 1927, Muslim League leaders evolved a compromise charter known as the 'Delhi Proposals'. They agreed to surrender separate electorates in exchange for joint electorates with specific reservation caps for Muslims at the center and in majority provinces.

qe: Which of the following demands formed a core component of the historic 'Delhi Proposals' formulated by the Muslim League in December 1927?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा मांग दिसंबर 1927 में मुस्लिम लीग द्वारा तैयार किए गए ऐतिहासिक 'दिल्ली प्रस्तावों' (Delhi Proposals) का एक मुख्य घटक था?
o: One-third representation to Muslims in the Central Legislative Assembly and the formation of three new Muslim-majority provinces
The immediate military annexation of the Kingdom of Nepal into the British territory
The complete operational closure of the newly established Dayal Singh College at Lahore
A total ban on lower-caste entry into public water bodies across the Bombay Presidency
e: Detailed Explanation: The Delhi Proposals laid down four key conditions: joint electorates with reserved seats, one-third representation for Muslims in the Central Assembly, representation in Punjab and Bengal proportional to population, and carving out three new Muslim-majority provinces: Sindh, Baluchistan, and the NWFP.

qe: A survey tracking path maps out a right-angled triangular layout from station O. A field vehicle drives 24 km North, and then turns to move 7 km East to reach target research checkpoint B. Find the absolute straight-line distance from O to B.
qh: एक अनुसंधान वाहन स्टेशन O से 24 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलता है, और फिर पूर्व की ओर 7 किमी जाकर अनुसंधान चेकपॉइंट B पर पहुँचता है। O से B की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 25 km
31 km
28 km
30 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial movement sets up a classic right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs of 24 km and 7 km. The straight-line distance represents the hypotenuse.
By applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{24^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{576 + 49} = \sqrt{625} = \mathbf{25\text{ km}}$.

qe: In a biological ecosystem study tracking energy metrics, if the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) of an alluvial biome is 44,000 units and the energy accumulated as Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is 24,000 units, calculate the energy spent during plant metabolic respiration (R).
qh: ऊर्जा मापदंडों का मानचित्रण करने वाले एक पारिस्थितिकी उत्पादकता सर्वेक्षण में, यदि एक मैदानी बायोम की सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (GPP) 44,000 इकाइयाँ है और शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) के रूप में संचित ऊर्जा 24,000 इकाइयाँ है, तो श्वसन (R) के दौरान खर्च की गई ऊर्जा की गणना करें।
o: 20,000 units
68,000 units
30,000 units
18,000 units
e:
Detailed Explanation: Utilizing the core ecological productivity relationship formula: $NPP = GPP - R$, we isolate respiration losses: $R = GPP - NPP$.
Substituting the given variables: $R = 44,000 - 24,000 = \mathbf{20,000\text{ units}}$.

qe: The All Parties Conference sub-committee finalized the historic Nehru Report in August 1928. What structural layout was designed for the provincial councils within this draft constitution?
qh: सर्वदलीय सम्मेलन की उप-समिति ने अगस्त 1928 में ऐतिहासिक नेहरू रिपोर्ट को अंतिम रूप दिया। इस मसौदा संविधान के भीतर प्रांतीय परिषदों के लिए कौन सा संरचनात्मक ढांचा तैयार किया गया था?
o: Provincial councils to have a 5-year tenure, headed by a Governor acting on the advice of a provincial executive council
Provincial legislative councils to be permanently abolished in favor of centralized central executive ordinances
The councils to be split on communal lines with separate electorates granted to all intermediate castes
The absolute subordination of all provincial administrative subject lists directly to the London British treasury
e: Detailed Explanation: For the provinces, the Nehru Report proposed a responsible governance model: local Provincial Councils would hold a fixed tenure of 5 years, and the provincial administration would be headed by a Governor who was bound to act on the advice of an executive council responsible to the local legislature.

qe: What macro-level shift occurred in the global strategic objectives of the British colonial authority in India during the late 19th century under the vice-royalties of Lytton, Dufferin, and Curzon?
qh: लॉर्ड लिटन, डफ़रिन और कर्ज़न के वायसराय काल के दौरान 19वीं शताब्दी के उत्तरार्ध में भारत में ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक सत्ता के वैश्विक रणनीतिक उद्देश्यों में कौन सा बड़े पैमाने पर परिवर्तन आया था?
o: A renewed upsurge of tight imperial control and reactionary imperialist ideology to secure British economic interests against political dangers
The systematic progress toward granting absolute provincial autonomy to popular Indian portfolios
The complete financial dismantling of all high-cost British capital investments inside the railway lines
A total structural abandonment of the policy of 'divide and rule' across all provinces
e: Detailed Explanation: Facing severe cut-throat economic competition from new industrial powers like the USA and Japan, the late 19th-century British Viceroyalties (especially under Lytton and Curzon) adopted an intensely reactionary imperialist ideology. Their main concern was consolidating imperial control to protect British commercial investments (like railways and plantations) against rising nationalist political dangers.

qe: Under the financial decentralization scheme introduced by Lord Lytton in 1877, which specific provincial revenue tracking heads were transferred directly to the control of provincial governments?
qh: 1877 में लॉर्ड लिटन द्वारा शुरू की गई वित्तीय विकेंद्रीकरण योजना के तहत, कौन से विशिष्ट प्रांतीय राजस्व ट्रैकिंग प्रमुख सीधे प्रांतीय सरकारों के नियंत्रण में स्थानांतरित किए गए थे?
o: Land revenue, excise, general administration, and law and justice
Customs duties, salt monopolies, and central maritime commissions exclusively
The printing of regional military bills and currency tracking parameters
The absolute control over international trade networks plying along the coasts
e: Detailed Explanation: In 1877, Lord Lytton expanded financial decentralization by transferring heads of expenditure like land revenue, excise, general administration, and law and justice to the provinces, along with a fixed share of provincial income derived from stamps and local income taxes.

qe: The 'Cornwallis Code' of 1793 brought a radical structural change in the colonial judicial administration by introducing which concept regarding European subjects?
qh: 1793 के 'कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड' ने यूरोपीय विषयों (European subjects) के संबंध में किस अवधारणा को पेश करके औपनिवेशिक न्यायिक प्रशासन में एक क्रांतिकारी संरचनात्मक बदलाव लाया?
o: It brought European subjects completely under the jurisdiction of the civil courts
It granted European subjects complete absolute immunity from all civil and criminal judicial trials
It mandated that European subjects could only be tried inside the lower Munsiff's courts managed by Indian officers
It completely barred European subjects from purchasing private property in land within the Bengal Presidency
e: Detailed Explanation: A major feature of the Cornwallis Code was that it brought European subjects under the jurisdiction of the civil courts for civil matters, ending their relative legal isolation from local administrative courts.

qe: In 1860, a judicial modification regulated the privileges of European subjects in India. What restriction did it place on judges of Indian origin regarding criminal cases?
qh: 1860 में, एक न्यायिक संशोधन ने भारत में यूरोपीय विषयों के विशेषाधिकारों को विनियमित किया। इसने आपराधिक मामलों के संबंध में भारतीय मूल के न्यायाधीशों पर कौन सा प्रतिबंध लगाया था?
o: No judge of an Indian origin could legally try a European subject in a criminal case
Indian judges were stripped of any original jurisdiction over civil property disputes involving Europeans
They were legally forced to refer all native criminal files directly to the local Munsiff benches
Indian judges were required to pass all their sentences strictly in classical European ciphers
e: Detailed Explanation: Reflecting the deeply rooted racial discrimination within the colonial legal architecture, a judicial regulation enacted in 1860 specified that while European subjects were brought under court jurisdiction, no judge of Indian origin possessed the legal authority to try a European subject in a criminal case.

qe: During the central executive guidelines of the Government of India Act, 1919, what specific bicameral houses replaced the old unicameral Imperial Legislative Council?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1919 के केंद्रीय कार्यकारी दिशानिर्देशों के तहत, किन विशिष्ट द्विसदनीय सदनों ने पुरानी एकसदनीय इंपीरियल लेजिस्लेटिव काउंसिल का स्थान लिया?
o: The Central Legislative Assembly (lower house) and the Council of State (upper house)
The House of Commons and the House of Lords structural branches
The British Indian Association and the All India Kisan Sabha chambers
The Sadar Diwani Adalat and the Sadar Nizamat legislative divisions
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1919 Act introduced a bicameral central legislature consisting of a lower house named the Central Legislative Assembly and an upper house named the Council of State, introducing the initial structural principle of a double-chamber parliament.

qe: The Royal Commission on Decentralization (1908) made a critical recommendation regarding the financial and administrative responsibilities of urban municipalities. What role did it suggest they should play in primary education?
qh: रॉयल कमीशन ऑन विकेंद्रीकरण (1908) ने शहरी नगर पालिकाओं की वित्तीय और प्रशासनिक जिम्मेदारियों के संबंध में एक महत्वपूर्ण सिफारिश की थी। इसने प्राथमिक शिक्षा में उनकी क्या भूमिका सुझाया था?
o: The municipalities might explicitly undertake the responsibility for primary education and, if willing, for middle vernacular schools
They should be completely barred from funding or managing any primary-level educational facilities locally
They were legally forced to route 100% of their primary school tax revenues directly to the Dayal Singh Trust in Lahore
The Commission suggested that municipalities should manage only high-cost advanced technical engineering universities
e: Detailed Explanation: To optimize local governance, the 1908 Decentralization Commission recommended that urban municipalities should explicitly take over the responsibility for funding and administering primary education and, if willing, middle vernacular schools, while being relieved of secondary education burdens.

qe: Under the structural guidelines of the Indian Councils Act of 1861, for emergency legislative purposes, the Viceroy was armed with the exclusive power to issue ordinances. What was the maximum validity period fixed for these ordinances?
qh: भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम 1861 के संरचनात्मक दिशानिर्देशों के तहत, आपातकालीन विधायी उद्देश्यों के लिए, वायसराय को अध्यादेश (ordinances) जारी करने की विशेष शक्ति दी गई थी। इन अध्यादेशों के लिए अधिकतम वैधता अवधि कितनी तय की गई थी?
o: 6 months validity
3 years validity
1 year validity
1 month validity
e: Detailed Explanation: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 empowered the Viceroy to issue temporary ordinances during emergencies without the concurrence of the Legislative Council. These ordinances were given a maximum legal validity period of 6 months.

qe: When the constitutional machinery broke down or impasse occurred under the Dyarchy system, who held the sovereign power to take over the administration of the transferred subjects in a province?
qh: द्वैध शासन प्रणाली के तहत संवैधानिक तंत्र के विफल होने या गतिरोध उत्पन्न होने पर, किसी प्रांत में हस्तांतरित विषयों का प्रशासन संभालने की संप्रभु शक्ति किसके पास थी?
o: The provincial Governor
The Central Legislative Assembly majority
The Secretary of State for India directly
The Chief Justice of the Federal Court room
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the Government of India Act of 1919, the Governor was the executive head of the province. In the event of a political crisis or a failure of the constitutional machinery, the Governor was armed with the absolute power to suspend the popular ministry and take direct charge of the Transferred subjects.

qe: The judicial structure introduced under Warren Hastings featured a highest court of civil appeal that functioned in Calcutta under a president and two members of the Supreme Council. What was this court called?
qh: वॉरेन हेस्टिंग्स के तहत शुरू की गई न्यायिक संरचना में दीवानी अपील की एक सर्वोच्च अदालत शामिल थी जो कलकत्ता में एक अध्यक्ष और सर्वोच्च परिषद के दो सदस्यों के तहत काम करती थी। इस अदालत को क्या कहा जाता था?
o: Sadar Diwani Adalat
Sadar Nizamat Adalat
District Diwani Adalat
Mayor's Court
e: Detailed Explanation: Warren Hastings organized the judiciary into a tiered structure. Appeals from the district-level civil courts (District Diwani Adalats) were referred directly to the highest civil appellate body, known as the Sadar Diwani Adalat, which functioned under the Governor-General and members of the Supreme Council in Calcutta.

qe: Under the judicial hierarchy organized by Lord Cornwallis, which court served as the immediate provincial court of appeal above the Zila Courts, managed by European judges?
qh: लॉर्ड कॉर्नवॉलिस द्वारा आयोजित न्यायिक पदानुक्रम के तहत, यूरोपीय न्यायाधीशों द्वारा प्रबंधित ज़िला न्यायालयों (Zila Courts) के ऊपर अपील की तत्काल प्रांतीय अदालत के रूप में कौन सी अदालत कार्य करती थी?
o: The four provincial Circuit Courts
The Sadar Diwani Adalat at Calcutta
The Registrar's Court room
The Munsiff's lower sub-divisional bench
e: Detailed Explanation: In the Cornwallis Code framework, if a party was dissatisfied with a decision passed by the District Judge in the Zila Court, they filed an appeal with one of the four provincial Circuit Courts (established at Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad, and Patna), which were managed by European judges.

qe: What structural reform did Lord Cornwallis introduce regarding the legal accountability of colonial government officials for actions done in their official capacity?
qh: लॉर्ड कॉर्नवॉलिस ने औपनिवेशिक सरकारी अधिकारियों की उनके आधिकारिक क्षमता में किए गए कार्यों के लिए कानूनी जवाबदेही के संबंध में कौन सा संरचनात्मक सुधार पेश किया था?
o: Government officials were made completely answerable to the civil courts for actions done in their official capacity
They were granted absolute lifetime immunity from any civil or criminal litigation oversight
They could only be tried inside secret military tribunals managed by the British Parliament directly
Their official actions were subject to mandatory verification and clearance by local village panchayats
e: Detailed Explanation: A groundbreaking feature of the Cornwallis Code of 1793 was the introduction of administrative legal accountability. It explicitly established that government officials could no longer claim sovereign immunity and were answerable to the civil courts for any actions or abuses committed in their official capacity.

qe: What definitive change did the Government of India Act of 1858 introduce regarding the supervisory control over the administration of India after the dissolution of the East India Company?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1858 ने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के विघटन के बाद भारत के प्रशासन पर पर्यवेक्षी नियंत्रण के संबंध में क्या निश्चित परिवर्तन किया?
o: The power to govern was transferred to the British Crown, to be wielded through a Secretary of State answerable to the British Parliament
The absolute command of revenues was handed directly to the non-official Indian members of the Legislative Council
The administration was completely subordinated to a newly created Federal Court based in Allahabad
The permanent legal re-establishment of the traditional Mughal legal system under a Deputy Nizam
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act of 1858 dissolved the East India Company and transferred governance directly to the British Crown. This power was exercised through a newly created cabinet post, the Secretary of State for India, who was assisted by a 15-member council and made directly answerable to the British Parliament.

qe: The 'Treaty of Sevres', signed in May 1920 between the Allied powers and Turkey, had what direct impact on the global status of the Ottoman caliphate, deeply incensing Indian Muslims?
qh: मई 1920 में मित्र देशों की शक्तियों और तुर्की के बीच हस्ताक्षरित 'सेवर्स की संधि' (Treaty of Sevres) का ओटोमन खलीफा की वैश्विक स्थिति पर क्या सीधा प्रभाव पड़ा, जिसने भारतीय मुसलमानों को गहरा नाराज कर दिया?
o: It completely dismembered the Ottoman Empire and finalized the removal of the Khalifa from power
It successfully extended the legal control of the Khalifa over all Muslim sacred places globally
It granted absolute sovereign independence to Turkey and its neighboring Arab territories unconditionally
It forced the British Treasury to pay all administrative salaries of the Secretary of State from London funds
e: Detailed Explanation: The Treaty of Sevres completely partitioned and dismembered the Ottoman Empire, stripping the Sultan of Turkey of his territories and removing him from power. This directly targeted the religious status of the Khalifa, which incensed Muslims worldwide and drove the Khilafat agitation into its mass non-cooperation phase.

qe: What retrogressive evaluation did the Simon Commission outline in its May 1930 report regarding the efficiency and financial management of local self-governing bodies since 1819?
qh: साइमन कमीशन ने मई 1930 की अपनी रिपोर्ट में 1819 के बाद से स्थानीय स्वशासी निकायों के कुशल और वित्तीय प्रबंधन के संबंध में कौन सा प्रतिगामी (retrogressive) मूल्यांकन प्रस्तुत किया था?
o: It claimed that the management of finances had deteriorated, and suggested the retrograde step of increasing provincial bureaucratic control over local bodies
It celebrated the village panchayats for successfully achieving absolute financial independence across all provinces
It demanded that 100% of local tax revenues must be channeled directly to support the All India Kisan Sabha
The Commission recommended the complete permanent legal abolition of the office of the district magistrate
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon Commission (May 1930) noted that the financial management of local bodies had deteriorated since the introduction of the 1919 reforms, pointing out a lack of progress in village panchayats. Instead of expanding democracy, it recommended a retrograde step: increasing tight provincial bureaucratic control over these local bodies in the name of efficiency.

qe: What macro-level transformation occurred to India's dynamic share of global manufacturing exports across the centuries of British colonial rule?
qh: ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के सदियों के दौरान वैश्विक विनिर्माण निर्यात (world manufacturing exports) में भारत कीं गतिशील हिस्सेदारी में बड़े पैमाने पर क्या परिवर्तन आया?
o: It dramatically fell from 27 per cent down to a mere 2 per cent
It increased steadily from 2 per cent up to an optimized 27 per cent
It remained perfectly constant at a balanced 10 per cent layout
It dropped to zero instantly within the first decade of the Charter Act of 1813
e: Detailed Explanation: As highlighted by modern economic historians, the systemic deindustrialization and forced commercialization under British rule caused India's share of world manufacturing exports to crash from a dominant 27 per cent down to a mere 2 per cent by the end of the colonial era.
